title: Phase I: Jazz Foundations (1910s–50s)
learning: Jazz harmony establishes the ii–V–I tension–release loop and the chromatic secondary dominants that power the Circle of Fifths.
The "triad of accompaniment" (piano, guitar, ukulele) evolves from stride and four-to-the-bar comping to walking bass plus shell voicings.
Rhythmic feel shifts from march-time Ragtime to swung eighths, codifying the ride-cymbal lilt and quarter-note bass lineage for later styles.

genres.name: Ragtime
genres.description: The rhythmic precursor to jazz. Syncopated right hand over a steady 'stride' left hand.
genres.progressionNote: Classic Circle-of-Fifths turnaround using secondary dominants (C–A7–D7–G7 → C).

progressionChords.note: Home base tonic. Often voiced as C6/CΔ for period-correct color.
Secondary dominant (V/V of V); pulls strongly toward D7.
Secondary dominant (V/V); sets up the true dominant G7.
Primary dominant resolving back to C; completes the circle.

instruments.piano: Stride: LH alternates low bass note (1 & 3) and mid-range chord (2 & 4).
instruments.guitar: Bass–chord pattern: thumb hits roots, fingers strum chords on off-beats.
instruments.ukulele: Split-strum: down on G/C, up on E/A to fake stride separation.

theoryNotes: Right hand often outlines chord tones with chromatic passing notes.
Left hand is basically an entire rhythm section – bass + comping.
Secondary dominants are your friend when you want motion without full modulation.

genres.name: Swing
genres.description: The dance era. Walking bass, swung 8ths, and the standard jazz ii–V–I grammar.
genres.progressionNote: The fundamental jazz phrase: functional harmony with root movement by 5ths.

progressionChords.note: Pre-dominant; smooth step up from I or vi.
Dominant that wants to resolve; often extended (9, 13).
Tonic resolution; can be voiced as C6 or Cmaj9.

instruments.piano: Shell voicings (3rd + 7th) with LH, fills in RH.
instruments.guitar: Freddie Green style: short, muted quarter-note chords on each beat.
instruments.ukulele: Triplet feel: down-up-down on each beat to imply swing subdivision.

theoryNotes: Bass usually walks in quarter notes outlining chord tones.
The drummer rides on cymbal with a 'ding-ding-da-ding' pattern.
ii–V–I is the default move: if you’re lost, aim for it.

genres.name: Bebop
genres.description: Virtuosic, harmonically dense jazz. Fast ii–V chains and tritone substitutions.
genres.progressionNote: Tritone substitutions and chromatic bass movement; almost every beat has a new tension.

progressionChords.note: Key center – but often quickly embellished or side-stepped.
Tritone sub; creates chromatic motion toward Dm7.
Tritone sub for G7, resolving back to I with maximum spice.

instruments.piano: Left hand plays sparse shells, right hand runs long 8th-note lines.
instruments.guitar: Single-note chromatic lines, enclosures around chord tones.
instruments.ukulele: Comp lightly; leave the shred to horns/piano.

genres.name: Modal Jazz
genres.description: Fewer chords, more space. Harmony lingers on modes instead of constant ii–V–I.
genres.progressionNote: The interest comes from modal color and phrasing, not chord changes.

progressionChords.note: Side-step up a half-step for contrast; then back to Dm7.

instruments.piano: Quartal 'So What' voicings (stacked 4ths) that slide around.
instruments.guitar: Long modal lines, less worry about changes.
instruments.ukulele: Open-string drones + modal riffs.

genres.name: Bossa Nova
genres.description: Cool jazz harmony on Brazilian rhythms. Essential DNA for City Pop and fusion.
genres.progressionNote: Jobim-style motion: II7 and ♭II7 act as secondary and tritone dominants.

progressionChords.note: Tonal center; voiced with 9/13 for lushness.
Secondary dominant hinting at modulation but often redirected.
Tritone sub functioning as dominant back to I.

instruments.piano: Syncopated voicings, 9ths and 13ths, soft dynamics.
instruments.guitar: Thumb on beats 1 & 3 (bass), fingers syncopate chords on &-of-2 and &-of-4.
instruments.ukulele: Clave-aware patterns with light syncopation.

genres.name: Cool Jazz
genres.description: West Coast chill: airy horns, brushed drums, and smooth ii–V–I lines.
genres.progressionNote: Standard jazz cadence but voiced with close-position 9ths for softness.

progressionChords.note: Gentle pre-dominant; use guide tones and 9.
Lightly accented dominant; often altered but still relaxed.
Soft landing with lush 9 on top.

instruments.piano: Sparse comping with quartal colors and lots of space.
instruments.guitar: Soft Freddie Green-style grips with added 9s.
instruments.ukulele: Featherlight swing strum on shell voicings.

genres.name: Hard Bop
genres.description: Earthy extension of bebop with blues heads and churchy turnarounds.
genres.progressionNote: Minor blues language with altered dominants and gospel cadences.

progressionChords.note: Tritone pull into the altered V.
Altered dominant for gritty resolution back to i.

instruments.piano: Horace Silver-style gospel shells and blues licks.
instruments.guitar: Aggressive downbeat comps; mix blues bends with bop lines.
instruments.ukulele: Punchy off-beat chops outlining tritone motion.

genres.name: Gypsy Jazz
genres.description: Django-inspired swing with percussive acoustic rhythm and rapid arpeggios.
genres.progressionNote: Minor circle-of-fifths turnaround with chromatic dominant color.

progressionChords.note: Minor tonic often voiced with 6 for vintage color.
Bright dominant, often embellished with #9 or b9.

instruments.piano: If present, doubles basslines and chromatic runs.
instruments.guitar: Relentless 'la pompe' rhythm on acoustic archtops plus rapid arpeggios.
instruments.ukulele: Short, percussive down-up pattern mirroring la pompe accents.

title: Phase II: Rhythm Evolution (50s–70s)
learning: Groove moves from triplet shuffle to straight or syncopated 16ths, centering the backbeat and "The One" as the primary driver of feel.
Bass becomes melodic (Motown) or hypnotically repetitive (deep funk), while guitars adopt percussive chanks and scratch patterns.
Harmonic motion often simplifies to vamps so rhythmic complexity and production layers can take the spotlight, paving the way for disco and boogie.

genres.name: Early R&B
genres.description: Bridge from swing to rock. Triplet shuffle grooves and blues forms.
genres.progressionNote: Standard 12-bar form using dominant chords on I, IV, and V.

progressionChords.note: Bluesy tonic; doesn’t resolve like a normal major I.
Dominant setting up either turnaround or tag.

instruments.piano: Rolling triplets in RH, bass figures in LH.
instruments.guitar: Double-stops, Chuck Berry-style riffs.
instruments.ukulele: Shuffle strum, accenting backbeats.

genres.name: Motown
genres.description: Pop songs with gospel harmony and hyper-melodic bass lines.
genres.progressionNote: Pop-gospel classic; extremely singable voice-leading.

progressionChords.note: Home base; often voiced as Eb6/Ebmaj9.
Relative minor; smooth drop from I.
Dominant; pushes back to I or into pre-chorus.

instruments.piano: Block chords with rhythmic stabs supporting drums.
instruments.guitar: Clean, choked chords on 2 and 4.
instruments.ukulele: Backbeat-focused pop strum.

genres.name: Deep Funk
genres.description: James Brown style. Everything revolves around ‘The One’.
genres.progressionNote: Harmony barely moves so rhythm, subdivision, and dynamics take over.

progressionChords.note: Funk grip. Played staccato, often with muted ghost notes.

instruments.piano: Clavinet-like stabs, rhythmic more than harmonic.
instruments.guitar: 16th-note 'scratch' patterns with E9 at the core of the groove.
instruments.ukulele: Muted percussive hits on off-beats.

theoryNotes: Kick drum and bass both slam beat 1; everything orbits that accent.
Space (rests) is as important as the notes.

genres.name: Ska
genres.description: Jamaican shuffle with guitar/piano hits on the offbeats and walking bass.
genres.progressionNote: Simple triadic harmony; energy comes from rhythm guitar chops.

instruments.piano: Short skank chords on the & of each beat.
instruments.guitar: Upstroke offbeat chops with light palm mute.
instruments.ukulele: Tight offbeat strum locking with hi-hat.

genres.name: Rocksteady
genres.description: Slower, more soulful evolution of ska with heavier bass presence.
genres.progressionNote: Classic pop loop translated to the Caribbean groove.

instruments.piano: Sparse, warm comps on 2 and 4.
instruments.guitar: Gentle offbeat chops with more sustain than ska.
instruments.ukulele: Laid-back strum with emphasis on backbeats.

genres.name: Reggae
genres.description: Backbeat-driven grooves with lots of space and syncopated bass.
genres.progressionNote: Pop-friendly harmony but drums emphasize beat 3 (one-drop).

instruments.piano: Bubble pattern on 2 and 4 with light staccato.
instruments.guitar: Short skank chords; mute quickly.
instruments.ukulele: Backbeat chops aligned with hi-hat and snare.

genres.name: Afrobeat
genres.description: Fela-inspired long-form jams with horn riffs, call-and-response, and political lyrics.
genres.progressionNote: Harmony stays static so rhythm section can interlock intricate patterns.

instruments.piano: Clave-informed polyrhythms reinforcing percussion.
instruments.guitar: Interlocking single-note riffs and palm-muted triads.
instruments.ukulele: Repeated ostinatos locking with shakers.

genres.name: P-Funk
genres.description: Parliament / Funkadelic cosmos: synth bass, chants, and psychedelic clav grooves.
genres.progressionNote: Static dominant vamp that occasionally jumps to IV for crowd response.

instruments.piano: Clavinet scratches with wah and syncopation.
instruments.guitar: Palm-muted 16th-note grids, occasional fuzz leads.
instruments.ukulele: Ghost-note heavy chanks on the upper strings.

genres.name: Boogie
genres.description: Bridge between funk and modern R&B: slap bass, electric piano, and early drum machines.
genres.progressionNote: Funked-up ii–V–I with synth bass hooks.

instruments.piano: Rhodes stabs with chorus and syncopated fills.
instruments.guitar: Bright chanks and octave riffs à la Shalamar.
instruments.ukulele: Muted 16th-note feel emphasizing groove over harmony.

genres.name: Disco
genres.description: Hi-hat, strings, four-on-the-floor kick, and octave bass lines.
genres.progressionNote: Minor key with bright borrowed major chords for lift.

progressionChords.note: Minor tonic, often with 9/11 for lushness.
Relative major color; brings light into the progression.
Dominant pulling back to i or to a new section.

instruments.piano: Octave stabs and syncopated chord hits.
instruments.guitar: Nile Rodgers-style constant 16th-note groove.
instruments.ukulele: Fast, light 8th/16th strums with strong accents.

title: Phase III: Fusion & Sophistication (70s–80s)
learning: Jazz harmony electrifies: slash chords, 11ths, and lush maj7/9 colors sit over rock drums and odd meters.
Studio polish and Rhodes textures define the West Coast / Yacht Rock aesthetic—smooth voice-leading with pop songcraft.
These harmonic palettes flow directly into City Pop and AOR, teaching how to keep complex chords listener-friendly.

genres.name: Jazz Fusion
genres.description: Electrified jazz: complex harmony and time over rock volumes.
genres.progressionNote: Upper-structure triads over bass notes create dense, modern sonorities.

progressionChords.note: F major triad over G bass; functions as G11 with suspended sound.

instruments.piano: Fender Rhodes or synth leads with extensions.
instruments.guitar: Overdriven solos, jazz vocabulary over rock backbeat.
instruments.ukulele: High chord voicings; texture over lead.

genres.name: Soft Rock
genres.description: Radio-friendly rock: vocals and chords over less aggressive drums.
genres.progressionNote: The 'axis of awesome' pop progression. Works in many styles.

progressionChords.note: Tonic; may be voiced as Gadd9 or G6.
Dominant function but often kept 'nice' (sus2, add9).
Relative minor; emotional but not heavy.

instruments.piano: Arpeggiated triads or block chords under vocal.
instruments.guitar: Strummed open chords, often with add9 and sus2.
instruments.ukulele: Straight pop strum, accenting 2 & 4.

genres.name: Yacht Rock
genres.description: West-Coast studio perfection: rich jazz-pop chords and smooth grooves.
genres.progressionNote: Common-tone voice leading keeps everything ultra smooth and floaty.

progressionChords.note: Shares 3 notes with Cmaj7; super smooth move.
Dominant with 9 and 13 – lush but still functional.

instruments.piano: Rhodes comping with syncopated broken chords.
instruments.guitar: Clean, chorus-y triads and partials.
instruments.ukulele: Extended chords (maj7, 9) where possible.

genres.name: Progressive Rock
genres.description: Rock meets classical/jazz forms: long songs, modulations, and pedal points.
genres.progressionNote: Modal harmony over ostinatos; sections often change meter and key.

instruments.piano: Hammond or Mellotron pads, thematic arpeggios.
instruments.guitar: Riff-based power chords with odd-meter accents.
instruments.ukulele: Simplified chord hits on strong beats for meter clarity.

genres.name: Latin Jazz Fusion
genres.description: Salsa and samba rhythms blended with jazz harmony and electric instruments.
genres.progressionNote: Minor ii–V–i flavored with clave phrasing and montuno piano figures.

instruments.piano: Montuno patterns locking to clave and tumbao bass.
instruments.guitar: Percussive comping with occasional jazz lines.
instruments.ukulele: Syncopated upper-structure triads on offbeats.

genres.name: Sophisti-Pop
genres.description: Glossy UK/Euro pop with jazz chords, sax hooks, and clean production.
genres.progressionNote: Jazz-pop cadence with suspended dominants to keep things smooth.

instruments.piano: Electric piano pads with tasteful reverb.
instruments.guitar: Clean chorus tones outlining 9/11 extensions.
instruments.ukulele: Light strums on maj7/add9 grips to keep shimmer.

genres.name: Italo Disco
genres.description: Synth-forward European disco with arpeggiators and dramatic minor hooks.
genres.progressionNote: Aeolian loop that supports endless synth melodies.

instruments.piano: Sequenced synth stabs and arps.
instruments.guitar: Occasional funk scratches layered under synths.
instruments.ukulele: Simple downbeat pulses doubling synth chords.

genres.name: New Wave / Synthpop
genres.description: Post-punk sheen: drum machines, gated reverb, and bright synth chords.
genres.progressionNote: Pop diatonic loop with robotic percussion layers.

instruments.piano: Synth pads with gated reverb stabs.
instruments.guitar: Chorus-soaked triads with palm-muted 8ths.
instruments.ukulele: Steady down-up pattern mirroring machine precision.

title: Phase IV: Japanese Evolution (70s–90s)
learning: Kayōkyoku and New Music morph into City Pop by fusing AOR, funk, disco, and bossa nova rhythms with high-fidelity production.
The Royal Road (IVmaj7–V7–iii7–vi) supplies endless sentimental motion; FM synths and slap bass modernize the jazz vocabulary.
Technopop, anime themes, and Shibuya-kei lean on precise sequencing, secondary dominants, and bold modulations for dramatic lift.

genres.name: City Pop
genres.description: Bubble-era Japanese sound: AOR + funk + disco + bossa harmony.
genres.progressionNote: The Royal Road (Oudou Shinkou): emotionally charged, endlessly loopable.

progressionChords.note: Starts away from tonic; feels like you entered mid-journey.
Tonic substitute – shares many tones with Cmaj7.
Melancholic landing spot that begs to loop back.

instruments.piano: FM synths + electric piano stabs on off-beats.
instruments.guitar: Crisp single-coil funk chords.
instruments.ukulele: Maj7/Maj9 shapes with syncopated strum.

theoryNotes: Royal Road is functionally IV–V–iii–vi; try it in any key.
Bass often outlines chord tones with disco/funk rhythms.

genres.name: Technopop
genres.description: YMO-style computerized pop. Extremely tight timing and synth textures.
genres.progressionNote: Harmony stays relatively simple so sound design can shine.

instruments.piano: Mostly sequenced synth parts and arps.
instruments.guitar: Sometimes absent or heavily processed.
instruments.ukulele: More of a texture than a core instrument here.

genres.name: Anime Music (Anison)
genres.description: High-energy intros and themes with modulations and big melodies.
genres.progression: I – V – vi – III – IV – I – IV – V
genres.progressionNote: Diatonic with occasional secondary dominants; modulations common at last chorus.

instruments.piano: Driving rhythmic support, octave figures, and countermelodies.
instruments.guitar: Rock rhythm + melodic leads.
instruments.ukulele: Melodic support or simplified chords.

genres.name: Kayōkyoku
genres.description: Pre-City Pop Japanese popular song: Showa-era melodies with Western harmony.
genres.progressionNote: Sentimental loop that set the stage for later Royal Road hooks.

instruments.piano: Orchestral-style block chords and countermelodies.
instruments.guitar: Clean strums supporting vocal melody.
instruments.ukulele: Gentle down-up pattern reinforcing harmony.

genres.name: Shibuya-kei
genres.description: Tokyo indie pop blending bossa nova, baroque pop, and sampling culture.
genres.progression: ii7 – V7 – Imaj7 with borrowed chords
genres.progressionNote: Jazz-pop cadences sprinkled with French pop and lounge-influenced modulations.

progressionChords.note: Smooth resolution, often followed by borrowed IVm.

instruments.piano: Wurlitzer/Rhodes comps plus sample chops.
instruments.guitar: 60s-style clean chords and melodic riffs.
instruments.ukulele: Bossa-inspired strums that match the lounge vibe.

genres.name: J-Fusion
genres.description: Casiopea/T-Square style virtuosic fusion with pristine production.
genres.progressionNote: Extended dominant language with bright Lydian and Mixolydian colors.

progressionChords.note: Dominant push into solos or modulations.

instruments.piano: Sparkling synth leads and Rhodes comping.
instruments.guitar: Fusion leads with chorus and precise staccato chords.
instruments.ukulele: Tight 16th-note support on upper extensions.

title: Phase V: Modern Derivatives (90s–Present)
learning: Neo-soul, lo-fi hip hop, and future funk recycle jazz extensions (9/11/13) with swung or "drunk" drums for warm nostalgia.
Sampling culture reframes ii–V–I cells into static loops, while sidechain compression and vinyl grit become rhythmic instruments.
Modern producers continue the City Pop lineage—sped-up Royal Road chops, lush pads, and relaxed humanized timing keep the sound alive.

genres.name: Neo-Soul
genres.description: Dilla-influenced drums, Rhodes keys, and min9 / min11 harmony.
genres.progressionNote: Two-chord vamps with heavy color tones. Feel > complexity.

progressionChords.note: Warm tonic, often voiced very close with clustered tones.
Subdominant color, keeps things floating and unresolved.

instruments.piano: Rhodes with tremolo, lazy behind-the-beat comping.
instruments.guitar: Thumb-over bass chords, lots of 9/11/13.
instruments.ukulele: Min9/min11 shapes where possible; soft fingerstyle.

theoryNotes: Kick and snare feel late; don’t quantize everything to the grid.

genres.name: Lo-Fi Hip Hop
genres.description: Study beats: dusty jazz chords, low-passed drums, vinyl textures.
genres.progressionNote: Jazz minor ii–V–i, but often looped without strong resolution.

progressionChords.note: Half-diminished ii; built from the Locrian mode.
Can be altered (♭9/#9/♭13) or left plain.
Minor tonic with rich color tones; classic lofi pad voicing.

instruments.piano: Detuned, low-passed chords with soft attacks.
instruments.guitar: Very simple shell voicings, lots of space.
instruments.ukulele: Soft thumb-only strums or broken chords.

genres.name: Future Funk
genres.description: Sped-up City Pop samples with sidechain compression and bright mix.
genres.progressionNote: Often chopped directly from City Pop Royal Road progressions and looped.

progressionChords.note: Bright source chord from original City Pop tracks.
Minor home base; often heavily sidechained.

instruments.piano: Mostly sampled; new parts are usually synth stabs.
instruments.guitar: Chopped Nile Rodgers-style loops.
instruments.ukulele: If used, keeps to rhythmic comping.

genres.name: Synthwave / Retrowave
genres.description: Retro-futurist pads, analog basslines, and tom-heavy drum machines.
genres.progressionNote: Classic 80s minor loop powering neon nostalgia.

instruments.piano: Synth pads and brassy stabs with long reverb.
instruments.guitar: Occasional chorus leads doubling melodies.
instruments.ukulele: Straight 8ths supporting pad harmony.

genres.name: K-Pop
genres.description: Hybrid pop production mixing trap drums, EDM builds, and bright major hooks.
genres.progression: I – V – vi – IV with rap breaks
genres.progressionNote: Sectional writing: key changes and drops are common.

instruments.piano: Plucky synth leads and supersaw pads.
instruments.guitar: Filtered funk chops layered with synth brass.
instruments.ukulele: Occasional bright strums in acoustic sections.

genres.name: Trap
genres.description: 808 subs, skittering hi-hats, and minor-key pads with minimal harmony.
genres.progressionNote: Looped minor triads under half-time drums and melodic vocals.

instruments.piano: Filtered minor pads and bell plucks.
instruments.guitar: Sparse melodic motifs or reversed samples.
instruments.ukulele: Soft arpeggios if used; keep space for vocals.

genres.name: EDM / House
genres.description: Club-focused grooves with sidechained pads and big builds/drops.
genres.progressionNote: Loop-friendly Aeolian cycle built for filters and risers.

instruments.piano: Sidechained saw pads and pluck leads.
instruments.guitar: Occasional disco-style octave riffs.
instruments.ukulele: Percussive chops in breakdowns for organic texture.

genres.name: Drum & Bass
genres.description: Amen breaks, heavy subs, and minor-mode pads at blistering tempos.
genres.progressionNote: Harmony stays static so drums and bass variations shine.

instruments.piano: Filtered pads and atmospheric textures.
instruments.guitar: Rare; occasional reverb-washed swells.
instruments.ukulele: Arp-like plucks during intros/outros.
